Bill.BriefDescription: Revising the duties of the family and children's ombudsman.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to duties of the family and children's ombudsman;and amending RCW 43.06A.030.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 43.06A.030 and 1996 c 131 s 4 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The ombudsman shall perform the following duties: (1) Provide information as appropriate on the rights andresponsibilities of individuals receiving family and children'sservices, and on the procedures for providing these services; (2) Investigate, upon his or her own initiative or upon receipt ofa complaint, an administrative act alleged to be contrary to law, rule,or policy, imposed without an adequate statement of reason, or based onirrelevant, immaterial, or erroneous grounds; however, the ombudsmanmay decline to investigate any complaint as provided by rules adoptedunder this chapter; (3) Monitor the procedures as established, implemented, andpracticed by the department to carry out its responsibilities indelivering family and children's services with a view toward p. 1 SB 5873appropriate preservation of families and ensuring children's health andsafety; (4) Review periodically the facilities and procedures of stateinstitutions serving children, and statelicensed facilities orresidences; (5) Assess individual casework of randomly chosen caseloadcarryingchild protective services and child welfare services employees of thedepartment of social and health services throughout the state.Casework reviewed must be from any currently open cases and casesclosed within the last year. (i) Assessment must address employee compliance with the following:(A) Employee training; (B) department policies and procedures; (C)state and federal law; (D) safety and risk assessment; and (E) caseinvestigation. (ii) Assessment must include caseload levels and access to clericalsupport. (b) Assess supervisors of caseloadcarrying child protectiveservices and child welfare services employees of the department forcompliance with: (i) Employee training requirements; (ii) departmentpolicies and procedures; (iii) state and federal law; (iv) criticalthinking and clinical analysis; (v) availability to and communicationwith staff; and (vi) accountability. (6) Recommend changes in ((the)) agency policies or procedures foraddressing the needs of families and children; (((6))) (7) Submit annually to the legislative children's oversightcommittee and to the governor by November 1 a report analyzing the workof the office including recommendations for changes in departmentpolicy, state law, or funding; (((7))) (8) Grant the legislative children's oversight committeeaccess to all relevant records in the possession of the ombudsmanunless prohibited by law; and (8) Adopt rules necessary to implement this chapter.
